From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@healthco.com>, Jake Winters <jake.winters@healthco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Mar 2028 15:23:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: HealthCo security checklist & cloud partner data boundaries

Hi Sarah / Jake — great to meet earlier. Quick post-call recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on scope for the security/compliance review.

What we covered (summary):
- HealthCo is evaluating Redwood for inference on customer-record workflows (PHI possible).
- Key compliance asks: SOC 2 (Type II), HIPAA scoping, data residency and encryption, and vendor subprocessor list.
- HealthCo engineering uses AWS (us-east-1), Snowflake for analytics, and Segment for event routing.

Agreed next steps (what we'll action this week):
1) HealthCo to confirm current SOC 2 status, HIPAA coverage, and any special retention rules. (Sarah / Jake)
2) HealthCo to share a simple data flow / vendor roster (cloud partners, ETL, storage). You mentioned a data map — please attach. (Sarah)
3) Redwood to kick off a brief security questionnaire and share our subprocessor roster for initial review. (Rishi / Mina)
4) If HIPAA applies, we'll flag the dedicated/private options and surface the BA agreement and encryption controls. (Marissa)

Attachments to expect from Redwood: initial subprocessor CSV + a short security questionnaire link.

I attached a 1-page recap of today's call. I also copied Rishi (security) and Marissa (legal) — they'll lead the compliance follow-up.

Thanks — Mina

--
Mina Haddad
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192

From: Sarah Li <sarah.li@healthco.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Jake Winters <jake.winters@healthco.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Mar 2028 17:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: HealthCo security checklist & cloud partner data boundaries

Thanks Mina — good recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- SOC 2: We have SOC 2 Type II in progress for our analytics environment; report expected Q4 2028. We currently have Type I for core infra.
- HIPAA: Yes, parts of the workflow handle PHI. We need BA/DAA conversation and confirmation on encryption at rest across all cloud partners.
- Data residency: Primary processing in us-east-1; backups replicated to us-west-2. No EU processing for this workload.
- Cloud/vendor roster (attached): AWS, Snowflake, Segment, SFTP vendor (BrightDrop), and a managed ETL partner (Streamline Analytics). I've attached a first-pass data flow map.

I'll also loop in procurement if we need contract-level details, but Jake can handle the procurement timeline.

Best — Sarah

--
Sarah Li
Security & Compliance Program Manager | HealthCo
sarah.li@healthco.com | (212) 555-0147

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Mar 2028 08:07:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Next steps: HealthCo security checklist & cloud partner data boundaries

Internal — quick coordination note after Sarah's reply and the data map:

1) Action: I will send HealthCo the abbreviated security questionnaire and our subprocessor CSV today. Questionnaire will be a secure link (see related link placeholder).
2) HIPAA: Because they confirmed PHI, we should mark this deal for BA engagement. Marissa, can you prepare our standard BAA + the specific encryption language for Snowflake and S3 replication?
3) Data flows: HealthCo uses Segment (event routing). Segment may be a critical subprocessor we need to call out and verify if event-level data contains identifiers. Ask: Mina / Sarah — can you confirm which events contain PHI or direct identifiers?
4) Risk note: Snowflake account-level features (e.g., data masking, object tagging) will be something we recommend. Also confirm if Streamline Analytics has any downstream access for derived data.

I'll attach the current subprocessor roster for review (small CSV). Once Sarah returns the questionnaire and confirms events with PHI, we can mark any high-risk subprocessors and propose mitigations (dedicated capacity, token filtering, encryption-in-transit at our side).

Rishi
Security Engineering Lead | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

- We'll prepare our standard BAA draft once we confirm the PHI event types and scope. If HealthCo needs specific contractual encryption controls, flag them now so we can include in the draft.
- Procurement: Jake, when you have a sense of target timeline and any SOC 2 report SLAs, share so we can align legal review cadence.

Next steps (from Redwood legal):

- Expectation from HealthCo: return questionnaire within 5 business days and note any subprocessors they deem high-risk.
